title: Active Recall & Fast Review Demo
subject: Demo
description: A quick 8-question sample deck demonstrating multiple-choice, true/false, and identification questions.

questions.question: Which study strategy produces stronger long-term retention than passive re-reading?
options: Highlighting every sentence in bright colors
Active recall (testing yourself without looking at notes)
Cramming all topics in one uninterrupted sitting
questions.answer: Active recall (testing yourself without looking at notes)
questions.explanation: Retrieving information from memory strengthens neural pathways far more effectively than passive review.

questions.question: Spaced repetition works by reviewing material just before you are about to forget it.
questions.explanation: Effortful retrieval right before forgetting resets the forgetting curve and extends retention intervals.

questions.question: What is the cognitive effect called when spacing study sessions over time beats massed cramming?
questions.explanation: The spacing effect (distributed practice) consistently outperforms massed practice across subjects.

questions.question: During a fast quiz session in QuickReview, which keys let you pick multiple-choice answers without reaching for the mouse?
options: Arrow Up and Arrow Down only
questions.explanation: Number keys 1-4 select options immediately, and Enter, Space, or ArrowRight advances to the next item.

questions.question: Feeling fluent while re-reading a textbook always means you can recall that information on an exam.
questions.explanation: This is the illusion of competence: recognition feels easy, but exams require unaided recall.

questions.question: Name the technique where you learn a concept deeply by explaining it in plain, simple language as if teaching a beginner.
questions.explanation: The Feynman technique exposes gaps in understanding whenever you struggle to simplify an idea.

questions.question: Once you finish a quiz round with a few mistakes, what is the fastest way to close those gaps?
options: Re-read the entire chapter from page one
Use Retry Missed Only to drill only the questions you got wrong
Delete your progress and stop studying
Only review questions you already got right
questions.answer: Use Retry Missed Only to drill only the questions you got wrong
questions.explanation: Focusing on missed items avoids wasting time on material you already know.

questions.question: Where should new reviewer JSON files be placed so QuickReview automatically discovers them?
questions.explanation: Any valid .json deck file added to src/data/decks/ is automatically loaded on startup.
